- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if recent prices are above 90.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >95), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect; apply a “cool-down” adjustment: subtract 3–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-based corrections; rely solely on price momentum and mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often overshoot downward after peaks, but true outcomes show more gradual decline; adjust downward by 1–3% per day for 5–7 days post-peak.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 7–10 days; apply a “decay filter” — reduce forecast by 2–4% per day for days 1–7, then stabilize.
- No sentiment-driven correction needed — sentiment is neutral (all 0.00) — so ignore sentiment-based heuristics.
